title: What is an Entry Point?
overview: An entry point is the first file that runs when a React Native application starts. It is responsible for registering the root component so React Native knows which component should be displayed first. In React Native CLI, the entry point is usually the index.js file.

example.title: Entry Point Flow
example.content: Application Starts → index.js Executes → App Component Loads → UI Appears

title: Understanding index.js
overview: The index.js file is the first JavaScript file executed when your application launches. Its main responsibility is to register the root component using AppRegistry. Every React Native application must have an entry point.

example.title: index.js Example

title: Understanding App.tsx
overview: App.tsx is the root component of your React Native application. It contains the UI that is displayed after the application starts. In larger applications, App.tsx usually initializes navigation, global providers, themes, and state management.

example.title: Simple App.tsx

title: Application Startup Flow
overview: When a React Native application starts, the native Android or iOS application launches first. It then executes index.js, which registers App.tsx. Finally, React Native renders the user interface on the screen.

example.title: Startup Flow
example.content:
Android/iOS Starts
      ↓
index.js Executes
      ↓
App.tsx Loads
      ↓
React Native Renders UI

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned what an entry point is, why index.js is important, how App.tsx works, and the complete application startup flow. These files form the foundation of every React Native application.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ index.js is the application's entry point.
✔ AppRegistry registers the root component.
✔ App.tsx is the root UI component.
✔ The application starts from the native platform and then loads React Native.
